finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.assumptions: The multiplication of chunkSize with SIZE can result in a negative value, leading to an allocation of 0 bytes. This may not be a direct injection point but is a potential issue with negative sizes.

parsed.refutation_attempt: The reported issue describes an OS command injection via negative chunkSize affecting malloc. The code at line 23 allocates memory using malloc, not executing an OS command; thus the CWE-78 classification is incorrect. Additionally, the function merge receives chunkSize as a parameter; in this snippet it is set to a constant in main, not from an untrusted source such as user input or network data. No checks for negative or overly large chunkSize are present, but the problem is a memory allocation issue (potential overflow or huge allocation), not command injection. Since the sink is malloc, not a system call or command execution, the finding is a false positive for OS command injection.

finding.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
finding.assumptions: The input_FileDesc can be manipulated by an attacker, leading to unexpected behavior or injection points.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked the entire code fragment for any system command execution functions such as system(), execve(), popen(), or other exec family calls. None were present. The sink identified (read) simply reads bytes into a buffer; it does not construct or execute a command string. No path exists from input_FileDesc to an OS command execution. Therefore, the claim of OS Command Injection does not apply.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.assumptions: The output_FileDesc can be manipulated by an attacker, leading to unexpected behavior or injection points.

parsed.refutation_attempt: 1) The sink is the write() system call, which only writes bytes to a file descriptor; it does not invoke the shell or execute a command string. 2) OS Command Injection requires constructing a command string that is passed to a shell or exec family function – none of that occurs in the code. 3) The reported source, output_FileDesc, is a file descriptor integer that would typically come from a trusted open() call; it is not part of user‑supplied data that could influence a command. 4) No execution path in this fragment ever turns user data into a command; therefore the claim of command injection is unfounded.
